title: Regression Translator
summary: SPSS Linear Regression output (Model Summary, ANOVA, Coefficients) → lm(), then the APA sentence, including what Sig. = .001 really means.
hints: `fit <- lm(morale_score ~ sleep_hours, data = sm)` and `fit_summary <- summary(fit)`. R² is `fit_summary$r.squared`; F and its df are in `fit_summary$fstatistic`.
SPSS's Beta: `coef(fit)[["sleep_hours"]] * sd(sm$sleep_hours) / sd(sm$morale_score)`. The p for F: `pf(F, df1, df2, lower.tail = FALSE)`.

`write_up <- sprintf("*F*(%s, %s) = %s, *p* %s, *R*² = %s, *b* = %s", f[["numdf"]], f[["dendf"]], fmt_num(f[["value"]]), fmt_p(p), fmt_bounded(fit_summary$r.squared), fmt_num(b))` with `f <- fit_summary$fstatistic`.

spss.syntax:
REGRESSION
  /STATISTICS COEFF OUTS R ANOVA
  /DEPENDENT morale_score
  /METHOD=ENTER sleep_hours.
